item.title: Oregon has 3 quarterbacks who could start Saturday. Illinois has a freshman who's never started before
item.description: The Oregon Ducks will face a team on Saturday with an even less desirable quarterback situation. Illinois (3-3, 1-2 Big Ten) quarterback Katin Houser suffered a broken hand that will sideline him for four to six weeks during a 38-37 overtime win over Michigan State on Oct. 10. Oregon has played its last two games without starting quarterback Dante Moore, who suffered a concussion in the second quarter of the Ducks’ 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. However, while Oregon can turn to junior Dylan Raiola — a Nebraska transfer with 23 career starts — and senior Brock Thomas, Illinois is relying on freshman quarterback Michael Clayton II, who will make his first start against the Ducks. A positive for Illinois is that Houser was injured before the team’s bye week, giving coach Bret Bielema two weeks to prepare Clayton. “It was just good timing,” Bielema told reporters during his Monday media session. Illinois is off to a disappointing start after going 9-4 in 2025 and 10-3 in 2024. The defense is below average, while the passing combination of Houser and wide receiver Collin Dixon is one of the nation’s best. Dixon is tied for third nationally with nine touchdown receptions. Illinois head coach Bret Bielema celebrates their overtime win over Michigan State as he walks off the field after an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026, in East Lansing, Mich. (AP Photo/Lon Horwedel) AP Photo/Lon Horwedel AP Photo/Lon Horwedel Now Illinois heads into Saturday’s game against a resurgent Oregon defense, trying to get Clayton up to speed. His performance against MSU elevated expectations. Houser left the game late in the third quarter with Illinois leading 23-10. Clayton completed 6 of 8 passes for 88 yards and two touchdowns. The final touchdown came in overtime on a 25-yard pass that put Illinois up 38-31. Sophomore quarterback Carson Boyd also played. He rushed once for seven yards but did not attempt a pass. Bielema and offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. both said Boyd could play against Oregon (4-2, 2-1), but Clayton is the starter. Usually, Bielema said, his starting quarterback gets a lot of rest during the bye week while the staff works on player development. Given Clayton and Boyd’s inexperience, both got valuable reps in practice last week. “I think those two guys in particular took advantage of every rep,” Bielema said. Bielema has leaned heavily on transfer quarterbacks during his six years at Illinois, including Houser. But that could change if Clayton, a former three-star recruit, earns the job. “I’ve said several times that hopefully the next starter comes from within our program,” Bielema said. Lunney said Clayton will be more prepared than he has in the past given the circumstances. item.title: Oregon QB Dante Moore ruled out for rest of 2026 season
item.description: Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore will miss the rest of the season, coach Dan Lanning announced Monday night. “I’m not anticipating him being back this season,” Lanning said. “Really got clarity for us this past week, for him,” Lanning added. “And I think if it were up to Dante in any shape, way, he would want to be out there playing for the guys. But, unfortunately, it’s not really up to Dante. It’s not really up to me. We can control the setting and practice where he’s able to do things for us, but that’s not always the case in the game.” Lanning said he expects Moore, who has run scout-team offense in practice, to fully recover. “That hasn’t changed,” Lanning said. “Definitely feel that way, but for him to be out there on the field for us right now, that’s not gonna happen.” Lanning added that Moore would remain involved with the team. “He’s still going to be a big part of this team and helping us move forward and find opportunities for us to be better,” Lanning said. Watch " Oregon Ducks QB Dante Moore to miss remainder of 2026 season " on YouTube Watch The announcement comes days after the reeling Ducks lost 21-10 at Illinois on Saturday in the third straight game Moore missed while in concussion protocol. Before the Illinois game, Moore told The Oregonian/OregonLive that he felt good but didn’t know if he’d return this season and was taking it “one day at a time.” “That’s all I can do,” he said. He then began throwing passes on the field in shorts and a sweatshirt. Saturday’s loss all but knocked Oregon (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) out of the national playoff picture and led Lanning to fire offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer on Sunday. Without Moore, Oregon scored 42 points over three games and lost twice while rotating between backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. item.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
item.description: EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished. Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season. “One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity,” sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said. After his team’s 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward. On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability. “I’ve been proud of the way that they’ve worked,” Lanning said. “I don’t see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that’s challenging, too, especially when you’re young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief.” Oregon linebacker Devon Jackson (#9) drops UCLA running back Wayne Knight (#3) for no gain as the No. 13 Ducks face the No. 21 Bruins in a Big Ten college football game at Autzen Stadium in Eugene on Saturday, Oct. 10, 2026. Sean Meagher/The Oregonian The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26. That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings. Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year’s semifinal squad. RELATED : Can the Ducks bounce back from UCLA loss? Experts release new Oregon vs. Nebraska predictions It’s not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn’t happened. “The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we’re winning or losing,” punter Bailey Ettridge said. “We haven’t let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we’ve handled them well.” Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team’s goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust. “If you can’t trust your teammate, then everything ain’t going to form in the way that it’s supposed to,” he said. This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team’s goal to get better instead of blaming one another. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon’s loss at Illinois and firing of OC Drew Mehringer
item.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — The Oregon Ducks (4-3, 2-2 Big Ten) suffered their worst loss of the season at Illinois on Saturday . The 21-10 defeat came against a marginal Illinois team that started a true freshman at quarterback, rushed for 225 yards, and held Oregon to two scoring drives. As a result, on Sunday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning announced the firing of offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer . What that means for the rest of the season remains to be seen. Mehringer had to contend with several key personnel issues, including starting quarterback Dante Moore missing three games while in concussion protocol. Here are 10 takeaways from Saturday’s game and the firing of Mehringer: 1. It feels like Mehringer is the scapegoat in this mess Criticizing play-calling is an armchair quarterback’s delight, but doing so under Oregon’s current circumstances is somewhat obtuse. Few teams excel without their starting quarterback. The next factor is an offensive line that was clearly mismanaged in the offseason after losing three starters to the NFL. Next is inconsistent play from backup quarterbacks Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. Then sprinkle in losing top wideout Jeremiah McClellan (broken foot) after three games, starting wide receiver Evan Stewart (undisclosed injury) for the last two games, and two more rotational wide receivers heading into Illinois. Does all of that excuse Mehringer for Oregon scoring just 42 points over the past three weeks? No. But those are a lot of obstacles for any offensive coordinator to overcome. Watch " Oregon football fires offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer " on YouTube Watch 2. Where does Lanning go from here? Lanning will probably announce his new offensive coordinator during his Monday press conference. He could promote from within to get through the season and then conduct a national search in the offseason. Or he may have someone in mind to take over now and beyond. Whatever Lanning decides, the next play-caller had better hope Moore returns, or little will change. 3. It could be time to add a veteran coach to the staff Lanning did well by hiring younger offensive coordinators, Kenny Dillingham and then Will Stein. But maybe it’s time to bring in an accomplished, seasoned veteran coach to add a new perspective to a relatively young staff. Someone with a track record of success as an offensive coordinator and maybe as a head coach. Someone like former Oregon coach Chip Kelly, Northwestern’s offensive coordinator. No, don’t expect Kelly to want to return to Oregon. But someone like him could fit perfectly. 4. The wide receiver situation After Saturday’s game, Raiola was asked twice how difficult it was to build timing with the receiving crew, which lacked McClellan, Stewart, and freshmen Messiah Hampton and Jalen Lott. item.description: A new head coach will roam the sidelines. A franchise icon will make his long-awaited return. An All-Star will begin his redemption tour. And a new ownership group will watch its first season opener from Paul Allen’s former seats along the Moda Center baseline. item.title: OSU's Legree leads nation in receiving as WSU clash looms
item.description: CORVALLIS — There may be no more appropriate way to describe Oregon State’s outrageously successful passing game this season than explosive. The Beavers lead the country in passing yards thanks in large part to 10 passes of 40-plus yards. Jesse Legree is responsible for eight of those catches, including all five of OSU’s 50-yard pass plays this season, making it no surprise that he leads the country in receiving yards and touchdowns entering this week’s matchup with Washington State. “You see him with ball in space, obviously taking the top off a number of times,” Washington State coach Kirby Moore said. “I think it’s about playing team defense. Obviously communication is going to be really important, where he’s at.” The Cougars (1-5, 0-2 Pac-12) have the No. 2 defense in the Pac-12 thus far and are having that success by keeping the top on their pass coverage. WSU has allowed 11 passes of 30-plus yards, which is tied for 129th nationally and nearly 10% of the passes it has allowed. However, opponents are not breaking through that mark often, with just four passes over 40 yards and none for more than 50, one of 30 teams yet to allow such a play this season. “We don’t want to let the verticals up,” Washington State safety Jaylen Smith said. “We take pride in (not) letting deep balls go. We always look to play top down and take away the deep routes first.” WSU defensive coordinator Trent Bray will be tasked with doing what nobody has been able to do yet this season: contain Legree. OSU offensive coordinator Mitch Dahlen has been creative in moving Legree around to prevent defenses from taking him away. Last week against San Diego State that included moving Legree into the backfield for a variety of plays. “People are going to try and hit him at the line of scrimmage,” Dahlen said. “They’re going to try and two-hand jam. If they’re going to try and two-hand jam, it’s like OK, how can I move this guy enough where you can’t do that? You put him in the backfield, unless you want to jump offsides and do it, you can’t do it that way. “That’s what we do a good job of as a staff, is moving him around where you can’t just put a safety over the top of him because if he’s in the backfield, what are you going to do there?” Even if the Cougars manage to limit Legree, the Beavers have shown they are more than capable of going elsewhere, with an outrageous 14 players catching passes last week. Aeryn Hampton (20 receptions for 245 yards) and tight ends Eric Olsen and DeCorion Temple each have at least 20 catches and Aaron Butler has four grabs for at least 20 yards. item.title: The 2026 season is somehow worse than the 2011 Colts
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - NOVEMBER 27: Peyton Manning and Curtis Painter #7 of the Indianapolis Colts sit on the bench in the final minute of the game against the Carolina Panthers at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 27, 2011 in Indianapolis, Indiana. The colts lost 27-19. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ah, 2011. To be young again. Fifteen years have passed since then and a thousand things have changed in the NFL. History doesn’t repeat itself, but it sure does rhyme. The 2026 season for the Colts is starting to look and feel a lot like that disastrous 2011 season when Peyton Manning missed the entire year. Somehow, some way, though, it might actually be worse. Let’s go back to where it all started. Kerry Collins was brought in off the street and proceeded to get lit up to open the season in Houston. Curtis Painter and Dan Orlovsky took it from there and produced a 2-14 season after an 0-13 start. Manning, Saturday, Clark, Addai, Garçon, Diem, Brackett, and many others were gone by 2012. It marked one of the darkest times in Colts franchise history. As dark as that season was, 2026 said, “Hold my beer.” You see, in 2012, the Colts were able to draft Andrew Luck. Remember? 2011 was the “Suck for Luck” year. There was an incredible consolation prize for being so bad. 2026? Well, it may not be as awful from a record or even on-the-field talent perspective, but it actually looks worse. Key players like Buckner, Nelson, and Downs are gone already. The departure of more names is sure to follow. Unlike the 2011 team, there is no positive mantra to pull the team through. There is no Luck coming to resurrect them. Heck, there isn’t even a first-round pick. That is what makes this year worse. It’s not about 2026 itself. It’s about the long-term effects. The future is murky. After 2011, there was a direction and goal during the season. This season sees the Colts treading water, or worse, drowning. Many more questions linger over the Colts now than in 2011. To make it worse, the answers aren’t as clear either. 2011 was a gut punch for a fanbase that was used to high-level winning. Watching Manning and others walk out the door was enough to make a grown man cry. There was hope and a direction forward, though. This year, 2026? What are we working towards? Where is the hope? What is the future? A stockpile of draft picks and Jonathan Taylor is about all there is to be excited for. From “Suck for Luck” to “Sucks to Suck,” 2026 seems to be worse than the worst Colts season in recent memory.

item.description: Chantelle Cameron (left) has lost just once in 24 fights [Getty Images] Chantelle Cameron will defend her light-middleweight world titles in a rematch against Mikaela Mayer on the undercard of Jake Paul's fight against Cedric Doumbe on 24 December. Britain's Cameron beat Mayer by unanimous decision in August in an engrossing encounter to add the WBA and WBC titles to her WBO belt. American Mayer, 36, disagreed with the decision, before an angry exchange of words between the pair, which opened up the possibility of a rematch. Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) has confirmed the second bout between the two rivals will serve as the co-main at the Coca Cola Arena on Christmas Eve in Dubai. MVP co-founder Paul takes on MMA fighter Doumbe in the main event in the American's first fight since being knocked out by Anthony Joshua last December. Cameron, 35, will be aiming for her 24th win in 25 professional fights, with her only defeat coming against Katie Taylor in 2023. "We agreed to the rematch before the first fight, so we both kept our word," said Cameron. "And now the rematch is on the biggest stage in boxing." Mayer has won 22 of her 25 professional fights, and is looking to reclaim her world titles. "Although I don't feel I performed to my highest potential, I've been working hard to fix the mistakes I made and I will 100% come back stronger," she said. A year ago, things started to improve for them as head coach Clark Lea promoted up Steve Gregory as a first time DC, and they ultimately finished the season allowing a respectable 22.8 points per game. item.title: IMG Academy basketball falls to hobbled SPIRE Academy in ATLAS League
item.description: SPIRE Academy boys basketball put on a clinic against IMG Academy in the ATLAS League, downing the Ascenders 90-63 without their any centers available on Nov. 12 in Bradenton. The game got chippy early, with both teams trying to set he tone physically right after tip-off. SPIRE's Moussa Kamissoko led the charge for his short-handed squad, and picked up a technical foul in the first quarter after scoring while getting fouled and addressing the IMG home crowd with gusto. From there, Kamissoko took over the game. When Mohamed Kieta briefly left the game after taking a hard fall in the first quarter, SPIRE seemed to be in very dire straits. Instead, Kammissoko shouldered the rebounding load and provided incredible help defense. The Syracuse commit tallied a game-high 14 boards with two blocks with 11 points. After trading haymakers in the first quarter, IMG held a 17-16 lead. The lead evaporated as the tempo picked up, and by halftime the Ascenders found themselves in a 42-28 hole. With no traditional bigs on the floor, SPIRE pushed the pace to the highest level. Everything got pushed up the floor, and SPIRE's guards were efficient with their paint touches. King Gibson went 10-of-20 from the floor and 4-of-6 from deep for a game-high 26 points. Darrell Davis sniffed a triple-double with 23 points, seven assists and six rebounds. With the tempo being pushed to the max, IMG got next to nothing from their bigs. Dylan Betts, the 7-foot-3 starter, finished with one point and largely did not play in the second half. His backup, the 7-2 Yahya Basaran, was 0-for-2 from the floor. Both registered just three rebounds. With SPIRE dictating the game, the Ascenders found no flow on offense. They coughed up 16 turnovers as a team, which SPIRE feasted on with a higher tempo. Malik Olajuwon led IMG with 13 points five assists, eight boards, two steals and a pair of blocks. Bentley Lusakueno tacked on 10 points and nine rebounds in the loss. item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: C.J. Henderson #26 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the New Orleans Saints at Caesars Superdome on October 5, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ian Cunningham is not sitting around and waiting to lock up players the Atlanta Falcons feel good about. In fact, he just got his second new contract of the day done with a Falcons defender. After the team reportedly locked up Cameron Thomas , they’ve signed veteran cornerback C.J. Henderson to a two-year deal. It’s well-deserved for a player who has gone from a first round bust in Jacksonville to a valuable starter in Atlanta, and it means Henderson will likely be in the starting mix at corner for 2027 and beyond. He’s earned it by battling his way up the depth chart here and beginning to really deliver on the promise that once made him a top pick. We've agreed to terms with C.J. Henderson on a two-year extension! https://t.co/eqXtHKagqn pic.twitter.com/yhz785gxMZ — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) November 13, 2026 Henderson was originally drafted ninth overall in 2020, ahead of fellow Falcons starter A.J. Terrell, and had an up-and-down tenure in Jacksonville that ended when the team shipped him off to Carolina alongside a fifth round pick for a third rounder and a backup tight end. Henderson was a part-time starter with more ups and downs from 2021 to 2023 with Carolina, and spent time with the Texans and Steelers before winding up on Atlanta’s practice squad. He did fine work in limited spot duty in 2025, but was pressed into more significant action with injuries piling up in 2026 and has been solid-to-stellar in every game except the rough matchup against the Bengals last week. For the year, Henderson has allowed just 54.5% of the passes thrown his way to be completed for 252 yards, 10.5 yards per reception, three touchdowns, and five pass breakups. That completion percentage is the lowest number allowed by any Falcons defensive back this year, and he’s kept his missed tackle rate low while only being penalized once. It’s a renaissance year for Henderson, who has the coaching staff’s trust and is at worst a very high-end backup for Atlanta that they can count on to start for extended stretches when called upon; I would not be surprised if he keeps his starting job all year. We don’t have the terms of the deal yet, but keeping Henderson around gives the Falcons a quality, deep cornerback corps well into 2028 with A.J. Terrell, Avieon Terrell, Billy Bowman Jr., Sydney Brown, and maybe Mike Hughes all here too. Congratulations to Henderson, and let’s hope he can keep this good thing going.

item.description: Heading into and now during the 2026 college football season, everyone has been talking about who is “this year’s Indiana,” or who is the “next Indiana” as a team that comes out of nowhere to find massive success. The simple fact is that, most years, there’s no Indiana. Most of the best teams in college football are programs that are consistently near the top of the sport, and breakthrough teams, especially ones that go 16-0, rarely happen. So while there may be no 2025 Indiana this season, there is a team that has extreme parallels to 2024 Indiana – Curt Cignetti’s first team in Bloomington. That team is the Wake Forest Demon Deacons, and they continue to be disrespected by the college football media while they are in the middle of their breakout. MORE: 4 biggest risers in College Football after Week 10 Wake Forest builds a winning program with limited resources Oct 3, 2026; Winston-Salem, North Carolina, USA; Wake Forest Demon Deacons head coach Jake Dickert leads his team onto the field against the Stanford Cardinal during the first half at Allegacy Federal Credit Union Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Through the 2010s, Wake Forest was an average-to-above-average ACC program under Dave Clawson. From 2016 to 2024, they averaged 6.8 wins per season (with the 2020 COVID season bringing that down slightly), and reached 7 straight bowl games from 2016 to 2022, winning five of them. They were always a program that had done more with less. Wake Forest, one of the smallest Power-4 institutions by enrollment and alumni base, was never going to be flush with cash or have the best resources and facilities. The high academic standards also limited the types of players Wake Forest could recruit. When Dave Clawson retired after the 2024 season, it was natural to question if Wake could continue this “winning with less” formula in the transfer portal and NIL era. In comes Jake Dickert. He was tabbed as the next Wake Forest head coach after an 8-4 regular season at Washington State (where his quarterback was John Mateer, which is not relevant to the story, but a cool factoid). Dickert had no East Coast connections, and the media questioned whether he was a one-year wonder in Pullman. But he immediately found success in Winston-Salem. He retained star RB Demond Claiborne, brought some key players from Washington State like WR Carlos Hernandez, and brought in QB Robby Ashford from the transfer portal. The Deacs surprised everyone in Dickert’s first year, finishing 9-4 with a Bowl Game victory. It was a career renaissance for Ashford, who Auburn and South Carolina fans will remind you was not good at all in the SEC. But heading into year two of the Dickert era, things weren’t looking optimistic. item.description: Pochettino in tears as he bids farewell to USA before Manchester United move Mauricio Pochettino was in tears as he addressed the media for the first time since deciding to leave the USA national team for Manchester United . Pochettino has agreed a deal to become Manchester United's head coach and will leave his role with the USA for the Premier League on November 18th. The Argentine signed a new contract with the US in the summer, after leading the co-hosts to the Round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup. Pochettino calls Manchester United move the “most difficult decision” of his career Speaking ahead of the Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti tomorrow evening, Pochettino said the decision was 'he most difficult' of his managerial career. “It's difficult to talk now. I'm an very emotional guy. It's a very sad decision, it’s the most difficult decision of my career," he said at a pre-game press conference. “But we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. "Normally it's the opposite. You're sacked and you cry because you want to stay. "For this case it's the opposite. It's a really tough decision, but at the same time I'm excited for that step. "The staff and the players, I want to say thank you so much for the last two years. You made me feel really happy sharing an amazing project. It's difficult now for me to finish. "We were very excited to share a project which we really believe in and are evolving together, it makes the decision harder. It's a sad decision but we are professionals, and we need to try to find the next step to make your dreams come true."

item.title: Drew Brees Admits He Wants ‘Monday Night Football’ Job if Troy Aikman Leaves ESPN
item.description: Drew Brees and Troy Aikman - Drew Brees and Troy Aikman (Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC; Perry Knotts/Getty Images) As Troy Aikman ’s future on Monday Night Football continues to hang in the balance, another potential successor is already raising his hand. In an exclusive interview with Front Office Sports , former New Orleans Saints quarterback and current Fox Sports analyst Drew Brees revealed that he would be interested in taking over ESPN ‘s broadcast booth if the seat opens up. Aikman is currently in the final year of his contract and has yet to receive an extension through ESPN, which has fueled speculation that his tenure next to play-by-play partner Joe Buck may come to an end following Super Bowl LXI. While speaking with Front Office Sports’ Baker Machado, Brees emphasized his appreciation for his current role at Fox while making it clear he wants to reach the top of sports broadcasting. “At the end of the day, I aspire to be the best at what I’m pursuing,” Brees told FOS. “I love broadcasting and I love my team. And I love being able to broadcast games every week.” Brees—who joined Fox full-time during the 2025 season—also spoke about how his comfort level has grown in the booth as he aspires for another broadcast role. “That’s my goal and aspiration, and that’s what I’m working towards,” Brees added. “Every week, I feel like it’s getting better and better and more comfortable. I love the crew that I work with at Fox. I think they’re absolute pros.” Related Is Tony Romo Set to Replace Troy Aikman at ESPN After Surprise 'MNF' Appearance? Of course, landing the Monday Night Footbal l analyst role would be no small feat. If ESPN moves on from Aikman, Brees would face a crowded field of rumored candidates. Earlier this month, The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand reported that ESPN is looking at Peyton Manning or Greg Olsen as their top choices to fill the role. FOS has also reported that the network’s wishlist includes other names like Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce . Others have even speculated that Tony Romo could fill Aikman’s shoes after his surprise appearance on Pat McAfee ‘s show earlier in the week. The speculation follows months of brewing behind-the-scenes friction, highlighted by reports of a tense verbal disagreemen t between Aikman and Buck at SoFi Stadium after Buck quietly inked a five-year, $108 million extension with ESPN. For now, it looks like Brees has officially thrown his hat into the ring, setting the stage for an aggressive offseason game of broadcast musical chairs. item.title: McNulty 'begged' England to make Whatmuff available
item.description: Stockport County boss Jimmy McNulty says he "begged" England Under-20 boss Darren Moore to free up Oliver Whatmuff to play in Saturday's match against Reading after the goalkeeper was called up for international duty. On-loan Manchester City stopper Whatmuff, 19, made his Under-20s debut in September against Italy and has since played for his country against France and Germany. He was brought on by McNulty during the first half of County's FA Cup comeback win in extra time against Isthmian League outfit Cray Wanderers on Sunday after stand-in Luca Ashby-Hammond had been sent off for a professional foul. The dismissal meant Ashby-Hammond is suspended for the League One visit of Reading and McNulty said after the Cray game that Whatmuff "led" the decision to withdraw from playing for his country. He was one of four players to withdraw from Moore's squad to play against Czechia and Portugal. "I called him [Darren Moore], begging him to help us out," McNulty told BBC Radio Manchester. Oliver Whatmuff spent last season on loan at Rochdale, where he also played under Jimmy McNulty as the club won promotion back to the Football League [Getty Images] "I know he's been a Football League manager, and to be fair to Darren, he's a lovely person, and he was very empathetic towards that situation. "He understood the conundrum we were faced with. We had planned for Luca [Ashby-Hammond] to play the games, but the red card changed all that. "We would have been exploring the emergency market had England, and Darren, not been so accommodating." Whatmuff, a highly-rated prospect at City, has made 15 appearances for Stockport this season, having quickly reunited with McNulty, for whom he played at Rochdale last term, helping them to promotion via the National League play-off final. "He [Oliver] was the guy who led it [the decision to withdraw]," McNulty added. "It means his heart is in the right place towards his team-mates. Essentially putting his team-mates here ahead of his country - I thought that was a brilliant sign of a squad that's together." County are sitting pretty in second place, and three points at the weekend would take them level on points at the summit with table-toppers Huddersfield. "We have a great respect for Leam [Richardson, Reading boss] and his team," McNulty added. "They're talented, they score a lot of goals, so [it's a game between] two attacking teams with slightly different dynamics. "I think it will be a very good game which should represent top League One quality from both teams." McNulty also confirmed defender Jay Mingi sustained a "very significant hamstring" injury against Cray on Sunday which has required surgery and he will be missing from first-team action for the foreseeable future. item.description: MILWAUKEE, WI - OCTOBER 30: Jake Bauers #9 of the Milwaukee Brewers celebrates during the 2026 World Series Parade of Champions at Henry Maier Festival Park on Friday, October 30, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Aaron Gash/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Welcome to the 2026-27 edition of Smash or Pass , in which we examine potential free agent and trade targets to determine whether the Red Sox should pursue them and what it would take to land them. Today, we continue the series with one of the heros of the 2026 postseason. Who is he and where does he come from? He’s Jake Bauers and he was born on October 6, 1995, which was the very day that the Mo Vaughn and John Valentin-led Red Sox were swept out of the playoffs by the juggernaut Cleveland Indians. Does that mean anything? Does Craig Breslow need to consult an astrologist before offering Bauers a contract? Would signing him open up some kind of wormhole underneath the plate at Fenway Park that would allow passage directly between the Charles and the River Styx? Because, if so, maybe we can just say “pass” right now. Is he any good? If you’re one of those Scottish footy fans who saw a baseball game for the first in your life back in June , then you may well think that Jake Bauers is one of the best baseball players on the planet. He was the best hitter on the best team in the world this year, combining power and patience in the heart of the Brewers lineup. In October, he broke containment and became one of the stars of the postseason, winning the NLCS MVP and doing so not necessarily with his power bat (he only hit one homer in the four-game sweep), but on the strength of his plate discipline. With 2 outs and 2 on in the bottom of the 3rd of game 2, as the Brewers trailed the Dodgers 2-1, it was Bauers who worked a 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto. It was the longest at-bat of Yamamoto’s career and it visibly tired out the Dodgers ace, leading to Christian Yelich’s subsequent go-ahead single and an early hook for Yamamoto. It was the turning point of the series, and if Bauers didn’t necessarily earn MVP honors on the back of that walk alone, he sealed it the next game when he worked an 11-pitch at-bat against Blake Snell, ending this one not with a walk but a go-ahead 2-run bomb. item.title: Pistons explain Ebuka Okorie's assignment to the G League
item.description: WASHINGTON — With Cade Cunningham in foul trouble and Daniss Jenkins needing a breather, coach J.B. Bickerstaff had no choice but to call on rookie guard Ebuka Okorie. The moment came at the start of the fourth quarter during the Detroit Pistons' 122-114 victory over the Washington Wizards on Monday, Nov. 9, inside Little Caesars Arena . Okorie played six minutes, the most significant playing time of his young career. He entered the game and quickly made an impact by scoring his first career field goal with an and-1 up-and-under layup. Taking full advantage of his minutes, Okorie finished the game with five points, shooting 2-for-3 from the field. At the time, Okorie's performance might've been enough to lay the groundwork for a spot in Bickerstaff's rotation. However, 48 hours later, the Pistons assigned Okorie to their G League affiliate, the Motor City Cruise. The decision doesn't stem from a lack of confidence, but from a desire to give Okorie more professional playing time. More: Cunningham scores career-high 52 to lead Pistons' double-overtime win vs. Wizards "We want to give him minutes wherever we can, and that has been the hard part," Bickerstaff said. "Where the rotation is, it is easy for anyone to get stagnant because you do not get actual game minutes. We just want to give him an opportunity to get on the floor. You saw the other night; he was ready to go and prepared to play. We just want to make sure that he stays ready." Okorie's short stint against the Wizards highlighted key attributes that made him a desired prospect, which motivated the Pistons to trade up and select him with the 17th pick in the 2026 NBA Draft . Led by president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon, the Pistons were impressed by his ability to quickly analyze plays and make decisions, whether as a playmaker or a scoring guard. The only downside to his performance against the Wizards was an ankle injury he suffered after stepping on a player’s foot. Bickerstaff said there is no set timetable for Okorie's return or his debut with the Cruise, but the team hopes to have him back on the court soon. Bickerstaff said that if not for the injury, he would have given Okorie more playing time. Since his debut against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 25 , Okorie's minutes have been sporadic, but each time the first-year prospect from Stanford stepped onto the court, he made a positive impact for Detroit. "He is a tempo pusher. He can get to the rim at will and is an elite-level finisher," Bickerstaff said. "Defensively, I love the fact that he takes on challenges. Okorie made his debut after replacing Isaiah Joe, who suffered a right hip contusion against the 76ers. However, Okorie's debut lasted less than two minutes.
